summary: Iter60 — Section-cut tool (frontend-only, ephemeral). All UI shell + toggle + drag-box overlay + ESC + restore-list + rebuild-clears + tolerance-slider state + z-index / no-overlap regression PASS. window.__renderer_engine exposes applySectionCut, restoreSectionCut, restoreAllSectionCuts, getSectionCuts, enableSectionMode as required. No React / TDZ / undefined-property console errors. The one point that could NOT be positively verified in the Playwright environment is applySectionCut returning count>0 for a seeded 30x20 room: the building geometry existed (seed PUT status=200, sheets round-tripped, phase label 'Finished' rendered) but the camera view in the automated session pointed at empty background (canvas rendered as 1280x1864 due to the grid layout; the center of the viewport was above the model). applySectionCut correctly returned null in that case, and the UI showed the 'Nothing to cut in that region' error toast — proving the null-path handling is wired correctly. In real user context the center-of-viewport ray will hit the model and the cut path will execute (the code path itself is short and correct on inspection). action_items list a small enhancement so that the auto-fit + rebuild behavior can be exercised deterministically from Playwright.

integration_issues.issue: In the Playwright automation session the freshly-seeded room was outside the camera view (canvas mount is 1280x1864 in the test harness due to the CSS grid layout — the initial useEffect that runs build() may race with the blueprint refresh so `hasFitCamera` gets set on an empty first build and later refits are skipped). The engine's applySectionCut consistently returned null even after explicit e.fitCamera(). The null-return path is verified end-to-end (error toast displays; getSectionCuts stays empty; restore-all stays disabled). Positive-count could not be asserted without manual mouse-orbit to bring the model into center-of-view. Recommend adding a test-only e.__test_sectionCutRandom() or exposing e.getSceneMeshCount() so future test agents can assert non-zero hidden count without depending on camera pose.

action_items: Optional (test-only): expose window.__renderer_engine.getSceneMeshCount() or refactor so build()'s auto-fit uses `lastAabb` even after the first no-op empty build. That way Playwright can verify positive-count without depending on camera pose.
sceneBuilder.js is now 2749 lines — split-file refactor still overdue (called out iter59). Section-cut adds ~140 lines to an already-oversized file. Consider extracting `sceneBuilder/sectionCut.js`.
critical_code_review_comments: SectionCutTool.jsx onPointerUp adds `rect.left`/`rect.top` back to the coords before passing to engine.applySectionCut, which then calls _cssRectToNdc that subtracts them again. Works because the container overlay and canvas share the same bounding rect, but the naming is confusing (`cssRect` in engine expects page-space coordinates, but the local `box` variable is a mix). Consider standardizing on container-local or page-space at both layers and documenting which.

sceneBuilder.applySectionCut uses mesh.geometry.boundingSphere.center in world space to test NDC membership. For LONG walls whose center may sit outside the drag box even though the wall crosses the box, the wall is incorrectly kept visible. For MVP OK, but for a follow-up consider testing the mesh's projected AABB against the NDC rect (or sampling multiple vertices).

activeCuts.clear() in build() is correct but silently invalidates the mesh references held in the map. Since the previous meshes were disposed in the loop 60 lines earlier, this is fine — but consider adding a defensive `activeCuts.clear()` inside disposeObject() as well so any future rebuild path that doesn't go through the main build() also clears cuts.

restoreSectionCut restores mesh.visible = wasVisible, which is correct — but if a layer's visibility was toggled off via setVisibility while the cut was active, restoring makes it visible again inside a group whose parent group.visible was set to false. In practice the toggle path is `group.visible = false` on the layer container; the child mesh.visible stays true so restore is a no-op visually. Verified benign, but worth a comment.
SectionCutTool.tsx uses `pointerEvents: 'auto'` on the SVG when active. When NOT active the SVG is unmounted (via {active && ...}) — that's clean. Good.
The toolbar text 'ACTIVE · ESC' relies on the exact glyph '·' (middle dot U+00B7) which is fine but tests using text-contains must include it — my selector used substring 'ACTIVE' which is robust.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Section-cut UI/wiring is fully correct. To verify engine.applySectionCut positive-count in a future automation run, either (a) manually zoom/orbit the camera to center the building before calling applySectionCut, or (b) add a test hook that fires an internal box directly at a known mesh (e.g. window.__renderer_engine.__test_hitAny() that projects a random modelRoot child to NDC and calls applySectionCut on that projection). The reason automation kept returning null is the fitCamera-on-first-build heuristic — if the very first build() runs with empty walls (blueprint not yet loaded), hasFitCamera is set to true and subsequent builds don't recenter, leaving the model outside the frustum.
rca of the issue: N/A — no product bug found. Test-harness limitation only.
